I have written a Lean 4 formalization that reduces the Erdos odd covering conjecture to a single analytic number theory sorry.
Current status:

  • The structural proof is formalized and compiles
  • The remaining gap is a specific analytic inequality concerning the asymptotic growth of certain arithmetic functions for odd moduli.
  • To protect the core reduction mechanism prior to publication, the repository is currently private

I am looking for an experienced number theorist to privately review the Lean code and the mathematical reduction.
The immidiate goals are verifying the analytic gap and securing an arXiv sponsorship.
Requesting arXiv endorsement publicly in an open forum is against arXiv policy, I believe.
I think publically requesting someone review your work, and privately asking for endorsement after said review is within the space of acceptable behavior from Arxiv's perspective?

FWIW I asked the ArXiv people and they said that public endorsement farming is not explicitly against the terms and conditions but they encouraged people to unrecommended people who did so and who were clearly AI-powered

Previous discussion- #new members > Question about arXiv endorsement (Lean 4 work)
Previous previous discussion- #maths > Knuth's Torus Decompositions (m=4, 6) @ 💬

OK, so not against policy, but not exactly welcomed either, at least under increasingly common circumstances (I'm not claiming Idan is in that circumstance, sight-unseen, no one can tell).

@Idan hackmon you might get more takers if people can check for themselves if they want to offer any help. Keeping the formalisation secret isn't a help, "To protect the core reduction mechanism prior to publication" is not exactly how people behave here or in mathematics. It's not like you need to patent this, or otherwise ensure you give a journal first rights to the mathematical ideas. If someone independently comes up with the same idea and puts it on the arXiv today, then you "come second". If you are public, people will know of your idea sooner. And surely you are aware that publication in mathematics takes a long time, right?
